findings.title: Recovery-code update reads wrong UserCredentialModel field
findings.body: CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential builds UserCredentialModel("",type,recoveryCodesJson) which puts the JSON in getValue(). BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential stores input.getChallengeResponse() as credentialData, which is null for this input. The result is a null/empty federated recovery-codes credential, so setup appears to succeed via hasRecoveryCodes() but later getCredentials/isValid deserialization fails. The provider should read input.getValue() (as the OTP branch does) or the helper should set challengeResponse.

findings.title: getCredentials NPE for unknown user
findings.body: getCredentials() does var myUser = getMyUser(user) and immediately dereferences myUser.recoveryCodes without a null check. All other methods (isConfiguredFor, isValid, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) guard against myUser==null. When the user is not in the map, this throws NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream, breaking credential listing for federated users.

findings.title: Exhausted federated recovery codes never removed
findings.body: On successful recovery-code login the code fetches the credential via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() which may be a federated (user-storage) credential, but exhaustion is handled with removeStoredCredentialById(). That API only deletes local DB credentials, not federated ones. For a user-storage credential the delete is a no-op/failure, the exhausted credential remains configured and the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action logic relies on a local delete that never happens.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes handed to user storage in plaintext
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential serializes generatedCodes (the raw printable codes) to JSON and passes them as the UserCredentialModel value to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(). The local path stores RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel with hashed codes, but the federated path persists raw codes in the external store. Any user-storage provider following this contract (as the test provider does) must store and compare plaintext codes, leaking reusable credentials outside the hashed local model.
